metadata.source: NASA Goddard Planetary Geodesy and Altimetry Data
metadata.dataset: High-Resolution LOLA Topography for Lunar South Pole Sites
metadata.azimuthConvention: Clockwise from local north; 0 degrees north, 90 degrees east, 180 degrees south, 270 degrees west
metadata.curvatureCorrection: Approximate spherical tangent-plane correction using distance squared divided by twice the effective lunar radius.
metadata.projectionAssumption: Local distances are approximated using the spherical polar stereographic scale factor.
metadata.horizonDistanceDefinition: Radial ground distance from the candidate origin to the centre of the DEM cell producing the maximum apparent terrain elevation angle.
metadata.terrainCellRepresentation: Each elevation value represents a 5 m x 5 m raster cell. The cell centre is used as the representative terrain location; the exact location of a terrain feature within the cell is unknown.
metadata.processing: DEM radial sampling at 5 m intervals, apparent elevation-angle calculation using DEM cell-centre distances, and per-azimuth raster coverage tracking.
metadata.uncertaintyProcessing: The TOTERR value is extracted from the same DEM cell that produces the maximum apparent terrain elevation angle. It is reported as elevation uncertainty in metres RMS and is not propagated into horizon-angle uncertainty.
limitations: Terrain coverage is restricted to the downloaded Site07 raster.
Incomplete azimuth rays must not be treated as complete terrain horizons.
Elevation products may contain interpolated pixels.
LDEC records LOLA measurement spots, not a complete measure of DEM accuracy.
The horizon calculation is an approximate spherical geometric model.
The local azimuth orientation must be verified against independent reference geometry before operational use.
Horizon distance refers to the representative DEM cell centre, not the exact location of a terrain feature.
The 5 m raster resolution limits the spatial precision of near-field horizon distances.
The horizon elevation angle is calculated relative to the candidate origin pixel elevation.
TOTERR represents elevation uncertainty and is not equivalent to horizon-angle uncertainty.
No uncertainty propagation into the horizon angle is performed.
No landing suitability score is calculated.
No Sun or Earth ephemeris comparison is performed in this processing step.
